Services

Repair services

Every job is registered by serial number, photographed on intake, and covered by a written estimate before any work begins.

Complete movement service

Complete movement service and repair, mechanical and quartz — disassembly, cleaning, lubrication, regulation and final timing check.

Authentication reports

Independent authentication report for luxury watches — hands-on inspection, photographs and a written opinion, before you buy or sell. This is an independent professional opinion, not a brand service: I am not affiliated with or endorsed by any manufacturer, and the brand always has the final word.

$100 flat · paid in advance

Case & bracelet refinishing

Case and bracelet refinishing that respects the original lines and finishes of the piece.

Crown, crystal & gaskets

Crown, crystal, and gasket replacement, plus broken screw extraction and movement repairs.

Battery & sealing

Battery replacement with gasket renewal, so the watch leaves sealed and documented.

Written estimates & reports

A written, itemized estimate before any work begins — accepted and signed electronically. A final report on delivery: work performed, parts replaced, condition returned.

For jewelry stores

How I work

You stay the face your customer trusts. I am your outside watchmaker: you receive the watch at your counter, I repair it at my own bench, and you deliver it back to your customer.

1

Registered intake

Every watch is registered by its serial number, with photographs of the watch exactly as received. Nothing is touched before it is documented.

2

Written estimate

Diagnosis and a detailed written estimate. The store — or the customer — accepts and signs it electronically before any work starts. No surprises afterwards.

3

Repair at my bench

The work is done by my hands, with photographs during the repair when the job calls for them. Parts are passed through at cost — no markup, ever.

4

Final check

Timing test and a complete review of the watch before it goes back.

5

Documented return

The watch returns to the store with its report: what was done, which parts were replaced, and the condition it is delivered in.

✦

Start with one watch

That is how my current store accounts began: one trial job, a clear written estimate, and an on-time delivery. Judge the work — not the pitch.

References available upon request.

The tool behind the bench

BenchBook

Every repair that crosses this bench is run on BenchBook — the job-management app I built for my own workshop. Each watch is registered by serial number, photographed on intake, covered by a written estimate the client signs electronically, and tracked through payments to delivery. It is the same system your store's jobs already live in — no lost paperwork, no guessing.

BenchBook is currently in its trial phase in my own workshop; a version for other watchmakers comes next.
